record.paper_title: Higher Rank Brill-Noether Theory and Coherent Systems: Open Questions
record.original_question: For coherent systems of type (n,d,k) on the projective line P^1, when is the interval I(n,d,k)={alpha | G(alpha;n,d,k) is nonempty} itself nonempty, and if I(n,d,k)=(alpha_m,alpha_M) with alpha_M possibly infinite, what are the endpoint values alpha_m and alpha_M?

evidence.quote: Question 6.1. When is I(n, d, k) non-empty? If I(n, d, k) 6= ∅ and we write I(n, d, k) =]αm, αM[, where αM can be ∞, what are the values of αm and αM?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{P}^1$ denote the projective line over an algebraically closed field. A coherent system of type $(n,d,k)$ on $\mathbb{P}^1$ is a pair $(E,V)$ where $E$ is a vector bundle on $\mathbb{P}^1$ of rank $n$ and degree $d$, and $V \subseteq H^0(E)$ is a linear subspace of dimension $k$. For a positive real parameter $\alpha > 0$, the $\alpha$-slope of a coherent system $(E,V)$ is defined by
$$\mu_\alpha(E,V) = \frac{d}{n} + \alpha\,\frac{k}{n}.$$
A coherent system $(E,V)$ is $\alpha$-stable if for every proper coherent subsystem $(E',V')$ (with $E' \subset E$ a subbundle and $V' \subseteq V \cap H^0(E')$),
$$\mu_\alpha(E',V') < \mu_\alpha(E,V).$$
Let $G(\alpha;n,d,k)$ denote the moduli space of $\alpha$-stable coherent systems of type $(n,d,k)$ on $\mathbb{P}^1$, and define
$$I(n,d,k) = \{\alpha > 0 \mid G(\alpha;n,d,k) \neq \emptyset\}.$$
It is known that $I(n,d,k)$, when nonempty, is an open interval $(\alpha_m, \alpha_M)$, where $\alpha_M$ may equal $+\infty$.

Determine, in terms of the integers $n$, $d$, $k$:
(a) necessary and sufficient conditions on $(n,d,k)$ for $I(n,d,k)$ to be nonempty;
(b) the explicit value of the lower endpoint $\alpha_m$;
(c) the explicit value of the upper endpoint $\alpha_M$ (allowing $+\infty$).
artifact.category_tag: Coherent systems and higher-rank Brill-Noether theory
artifact.status_search_result: A 2020 paper by Newstead and Teixidor i Bigas on coherent systems on the projective line studies existence problems for $(n,d,k)$ with $k > n$ but reviews mainly known cases for small numbers of sections, and the survey itself lists this as an open question. No source confirms a complete general determination of the endpoints $\alpha_m$ and $\alpha_M$ or full nonemptiness criteria for arbitrary $(n,d,k)$.

status_evidence.title: Coherent systems on the projective line (arXiv:2001.07114)
status_evidence.snippet: our main purpose is to study the existence problem for stable coherent systems on the projective line when the number of sections is larger than the rank. We include a review of known results, mostly for a small number of sections.
status_evidence.claim: The existence problem for coherent systems on P^1 has only been resolved in partial cases, mostly for small k.

status_evidence.title: Higher rank Brill-Noether theory and coherent systems: open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Question 6.1. When is I(n,d,k) non-empty? ... what are the values of alpha_m and alpha_M?
status_evidence.claim: This determination of nonemptiness and endpoints is explicitly listed as an open question in a 2022 survey on coherent systems.
